articles.title: Over 1,500 protestors detained across Delhi, CJP leaders shifted to different locations - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Over 1,500 protestors detained across Delhi, CJP leaders shifted to different locations
Over 1,500 detained as Delhi Police steps up security
The detentions come amid an extensive security operation ahead of the CJP’s planned ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ demonstration, which seeks Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Delhi Police had earlier denied permission for the protest, citing concerns over public safety, traffic management and law and order.
Officials also pointed to the CJP’s application being submitted fewer than 10 days before the proposed demonstration and alleged non-compliance with conditions during an earlier agitation.
CJP leaders detained at airport, Dhruv Rathee picked up from home
Dipke, Das and Ranka were detained aboard their flight after landing in Delhi. A video shared by the party showed Dipke challenging the police to arrest him, questioning the grounds for the action and asking male officers to come forward as women personnel surrounded him.
Delhi under security blanket ahead of Jantar Mantar protest
Delhi Police had planned to deploy around 35,000 personnel from the force and paramilitary units, with checkpoints and barricades set up across the capital. Mobile internet services were suspended in parts of central Delhi, while entry and exit at several Metro stations were restricted.
More than 250 train services, including 179 local trains and over 75 long-distance mail and express trains, were also cancelled or affected amid concerns over traffic congestion around New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations.
The CJP has maintained that it intends to continue its campaign for free and fair elections and is demanding the scrapping of the SIR exercise and the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner.

articles.title: Delhi Police Denies Permission for CJP’s Proposed October 10 Protest at Jantar Mantar - Business Upturn
articles.full_text:
Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar on October 10, citing short notice, previous non-compliance with directions and concerns over public safety, law and order and traffic management. The decision was communicated through an official order issued on October 9.
Delhi Police Joint Commissioner Nupur Prasad said applications for protests or other programmes at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days in advance. The CJP had submitted its communication on October 7, which the police said was an intimation rather than a duly submitted application seeking permission.
The police also said the CJP had been granted permission for a previous protest at the venue but had failed to comply with prescribed guidelines and undertakings. The decision was taken in view of the prevailing law-and-order situation, public safety and traffic regulations in the New Delhi area.
Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita are currently in force in parts of central Delhi, imposing restrictions to maintain public safety and law and order. Delhi Police said the proposed gathering was being planned without the requisite permission and that the request could not be granted in the larger public interest.
The proposed protest was part of the CJP’s campaign demanding accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The Delhi Police said the right to protest is a fundamental right, but authorities must also consider the rights of other citizens, public safety and the maintenance of law and order while granting permission.
